problem:
Given that $det(A)=det(B),$ which of the following elementary row operations transforms matrix $A$ to matrix $B,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]?
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Row and Column Operations on Determinants

feedback.problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Given that $X$ and $Y$ are row equivalent matrices and $det(X)=-8$, find $det(Y).$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -6 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}],\,Y=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ -6 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $Y$ can be obtained from $X$ by swapping the $2$nd and the $3$rd rows. 

This changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.
Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Y) & =-det(X) \\  & =-(-8) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
